business_type_notes: Every grooming category is C (pet service) per the calibration pack, section 2: the groom is sold as an appointment the owner books again, not a quote. Inside C most cards are care or routine led (the coat's needs and what happens when the routine slips); Puppy grooming, Mobile dog grooming and any card about a nervous, elderly or dryer shy dog are behaviour led (how the dog copes and the handling principle that helps, never a promise the dog will come to enjoy it). The split is written into the card briefs, not into a type. Pet Sitter is C too, but the library excludes every Pet Sitter row (Pet Care niche), so that tab makes no pages. The quote wording is kept where code expects it: QUOTE_FREE on a groomer means the price is given free before booking, never a free groom.

steps.title: Tell Us About Your Dog
steps.brief: How to get in touch and what is useful to say first: the breed or coat type, the dog's age, how it copes with being handled, what they want from the groom, and a photo of the coat if they have one. No promise of a reply time unless [CV: response_time] is set.

steps.title: We Check the Coat and Agree the Groom
steps.brief: The look at the coat and the dog before anything is done (the trade facts stages: consultation and coat assessment), and what is agreed with the owner first: the trim, and a short clip where mats sit against the skin, which is agreed separately as recommended practice. Follows [CV: quote_method]; only say the price is written if quote_method says so. A consent form only when the client confirms one. Never restates 'free' (FAQ 5 owns it). Never promise how the dog will behave.

steps.title: Regular Appointments to Suit Your Dog
steps.brief: The first appointment goes in the diary on a day that suits the owner. A regular pattern following on only when the maintenance_schedule practice is confirmed or [CV: visit_frequency_options] is set; the trade facts give no single interval for every coat, so never name one otherwise. Never mention the price or changes to the groom (step 2 and Why choose us own them). Never restates the start time (FAQ 4 owns it).

step_2_no_visit.title: We Agree the Groom and the Price
step_2_no_visit.brief: Say what the groom will cover and that the price is agreed before any work starts only when the price_agreed_before_work practice is confirmed. Describe how the price is reached only from [CV: quote_method]; when quote_method is blank, name no method at all (no photos, call, video or visit). Only say the price is written if quote_method says so. A short clip where mats sit against the skin is agreed with the owner first, as recommended practice. Never restates 'free' (FAQ 5 owns it).

faq_slots.question: Are you insured to look after my dog?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The cover figure from [CV: insurance_cover] and what the cover is for: the dogs in the business's care, as the policy names it. Never what it pays or who it covers beyond that. Nothing about vehicle cover unless the client values give it.

faq_slots.question: What happens if something goes wrong during a groom?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: complaints_process] only. Where nothing is on file, say what the owner does: tell us and we look at it, and leave it there. Never invent insurance or a guarantee.

faq_slots.question: Do you guarantee your grooming?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Used only when a guarantee is confirmed in [CV: guarantee_years] or [CV: guarantee_scope]. Start with yes, then the terms. No claim about the coat's regrowth, and none about the dog's behaviour at its next visit.

faq_slots.question: What if my dog doesn't settle?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Used when nothing in cover_chain is confirmed. Open with what happens: the groom slows down, takes a break or stops rather than forcing the dog, and the owner is called, as the way careful groomers work, drawn from the trade facts rows (no dog left on its own, a groom halted and the dog made safe, the owner phoned). Principles, never this business's practice unless a confirmed practice says so. Then what the owner does: tell us before the appointment how the dog copes. No guarantee of a calm dog, now or at a later visit. Never sedation.

faq_slots.question: Do you have availability for new dogs?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: start_time] only, as given. No waiting list, no 'book early', no season unless the client values say so.

faq_slots.question: Can I get a price before I book?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [QUOTE_FREE] and [CV: quote_method]: the price is given free before the booking, by the method on file. Never a free groom. What can change the price on the day (the coat as found) only from the trade facts price rows, said once.

faq_slots.question: How do you work out the price for my dog?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: quote_method] only. What can change the price on the day (the coat as found) only from the trade facts price rows, said once.

faq_slots.question: How often should my dog be groomed?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The coat decides it, and the trade facts rows give no single interval for every dog: say so. Then the coat types in plain words, each with what happens between grooms (a coat that never stops growing and mats, a double coat that drops its undercoat, a wire coat that holds its dead coat until it is pulled, a short coat that mostly needs a bath and nails). A frequency only from [CV: visit_frequency_options]; otherwise say the pattern is agreed for the dog.

faq_slots.question: Why does my dog's coat keep matting?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Use the assigned symptom's meaning and its linked local issue. Three genuinely different causes in plain words: the coat rubbing where it moves (where ear meets head, along the collar line, under the front legs), a coat that gets wet and is not dried through to the skin, and brushing that only reaches the top of the coat. Then what the local walks add (mud, sand, long grass), then the fix: combing out where the mats are loose, and a close clip as the gentler route once they have tightened onto the skin, from the trade facts matted coat row. Never the owner's failure.

faq_slots.question: Should I have my dog shaved for the summer?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts double coat row only: routine shaving of a double coat to cool the dog or stop shedding is advised against, because the coat shields the skin from the sun and keeps the dog's temperature steady, and it may grow back differently; taking the loose undercoat out is the usual approach. Put the reason in fresh words of your own: nothing about insulating against heat and cold. Matting or a vet's reason can change the choice. Never a promise about regrowth, never a figure.

faq_slots.question: When can a puppy have its first groom?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts puppy rows only: no first groom age and no set wait after vaccinations is laid down, so give none. What a first session is for instead: getting the puppy used to the table, the brush and the dryer in short sessions, with the vaccination status asked about first. Never a figure, never a vet's advice on vaccines.

cards.title: Knots that have reached the skin
cards.brief: Tangles where ear meets head, along the collar line and under the front legs, pulling tighter with every wet walk. The one cause this card makes: the coat rubbing where it moves, and tightening when it gets wet and is not dried through. Care led. Say what the fix usually involves in plain words: combing through while the tangles are still loose, and a close clip to start again as the gentler route once they have tightened onto the skin, agreed with the owner first (the trade facts matted coat row). Link the Full groom page where LINKABLE PAGES has one. Never combing out tight mats written up as gentler than clipping, never the owner's failure, never a promise about regrowth. Not shedding: card 2 owns that.
cards.mechanism: the coat rubbing where it moves and tightening when wet

cards.title: Hair on everything
cards.brief: Loose hair on clothes and furniture, a coat that feels packed, brushing that barely touches it. The one cause this card makes: a double coat dropping its undercoat in heavy spells, as the weather warms in spring and again in autumn (the pack's seasonal note). Care led. Say what gets the undercoat out, from the trade facts deshedding stages: a bath, a dryer and the combs that lift the loosened undercoat clear. Then that shaving the coat off is not the answer and does not stop the shedding (the trade facts double coat row), without lecturing. Link the Deshedding page where LINKABLE PAGES has one. Not matting: card 1 owns that.
cards.mechanism: a double coat dropping its undercoat

cards.title: Dogs who find the salon hard
cards.brief: A dog that shakes from the car park, a dog that hates the dryer, an older dog that is stiff on the table, a puppy that has never been held still. The one cause this card makes: too much at once: a strange room, other dogs, the noise of the dryer, being held. Behaviour led. Say what good handling does in plain words: a pause to let the dog settle, rests part way, calling a halt instead of holding on, no dog left alone, from the trade facts rows as how careful groomers work, never as this business's practice unless a confirmed practice or [CV: materials_methods] says so. Where LINKABLE PAGES has Puppy grooming or Mobile dog grooming, link one as the route that suits such dogs. No guarantee of a calm dog, now or at a later visit. Never sedation.
cards.mechanism: too much at once for the dog

cards.title: Smelling of dog again within days
cards.brief: A coat that smells again soon after bath day, damp to the touch deep down, flaky or itchy underneath. The one cause this card makes: a thick coat not dried through to the skin, so damp sits at the roots. Care led. Say what washing and drying done well involves from the trade facts bath stages: the rinse, then drying done under supervision until the coat is dry at the skin, not just on top. A smell coming off the ears, the breath or a single patch of skin belongs with a vet rather than another bath: say so plainly, and never name a condition. Link the client's bath service page (its name in LINKABLE PAGES) where there is one.
cards.mechanism: a coat not dried through to the skin

cards.title: The size of the dog and the coat
cards.brief: A bigger dog, or more coat to brush, bath, dry and clip, takes longer: the first factor in the trade facts price rows. Say it plainly, coat type as the reason (a thick double coat against a short smooth one), and give no figure.

cards.title: The coat on the day
cards.brief: A maintained coat is a shorter groom than a coat with mats, packed undercoat or dirt worked in, from the trade facts price rows. Say that the coat is looked at before the price is settled, from [CV: quote_method] only, and that a short clip for a matted coat is agreed with the owner first. Never a word that shames the coat.

cards.title: Hand stripping and scissor work
cards.brief: Hand stripping a wiry coat patch by patch, or a long scissored trim, takes longer than a clip: the trade facts price rows for Full groom and Hand stripping. Say why in plain words (every patch worked by hand) and name the service only where the client offers it. No figure.

cards.title: The time your dog needs
cards.brief: A nervous, elderly or first time dog is groomed with breaks and more handling, which takes longer: the trade facts price rows. Say it as the dog's needs, never as a surcharge for a difficult dog. Code adds the price line from [CV: price_list] when there is one.

problem_card.title: What this season's walks leave in the coat
problem_card.brief: The pack's coat year, for the season the page is written in: undercoat shedding heavily as the weather warms and again as it cools, seeds caught in ears, feathering and toes through the warm months, mud and grit packed into the feet in the cold months. The one cause this card makes: the season's walks leaving something in the coat that brushing at home does not reach. Say what the groom checks and clears for that season from the trade facts stages (the brush out, the rinse, the paw check), and root that cause in the coat itself or in the dog itself, never 'a busy time of year'. Never a parasite, a tick outbreak or a skin condition. Not matting (card 1) and not shedding as such (card 2).
problem_card.mechanism: the season's walks leaving something in the coat

faq_slot.question: Does the time of year change what my dog needs?
faq_slot.answer_brief: Yes, through the coat: the undercoat coming away as the weather warms and again as it cools, seeds in the warm months, mud and grit in the cold ones, as the pack's seasonal note has it, each with what the groom does about it. The summer shave question from the trade facts double coat row only: routine shaving is advised against and taking the undercoat out is the usual approach. No dates, no promise of a slot.

items.title: Brushing out and checking for knots

items.title: The bath and the rinse

items.title: Drying, done under supervision
items.brief: The drying stage from the trade facts: dried through, the dog watched the whole time. A drying cabinet only from [CV: materials_methods], and never unattended.

items.title: The main work: the clip, the strip, the comb out or the trim
items.brief: The central stage from the trade facts for this service, named as the trade names it: the clip and scissor, the dead coat pulled by hand, the released undercoat combed out, nails taken back in small amounts, the teeth brushed on the surfaces the dog allows.

items.title: Nails, ears and the finishing checks, as agreed
items.brief: The agreed extras from the trade facts stages: nails, the outside of the ears, the final check of skin and coat. Only what the rows give; never work inside the ear, never anal glands.

items.title: A word about anything we noticed
items.brief: The handover from the trade facts: what was done and anything seen on the skin, the nails or the teeth that the owner might want a vet to look at. Observed and reported, never diagnosed.

items.title: The next appointment, if you want one
items.brief: Only from [CV: visit_frequency_options] or the maintenance_schedule practice; when neither is set, write that the next appointment is agreed with you and name no interval.

cards.title: The signs it's time
cards.brief: What the owner notices, from the trade facts signs row for this service, in their words (nails clicking on the floor, knots behind the ears, hair on the sofa, a wiry coat gone soft and pale). The one cause this card makes: the routine slipping between appointments. Care led. Then what it leads to if left, from the skipped row: specific, never alarming, and never implying the reader's dog has it. Never the owner's failure.

cards.title: Puppies, older dogs and nervous dogs
cards.brief: How this service is paced for a dog that finds grooming hard: short sessions, rests part way, calling a halt instead of pressing on, no dog left alone, from the trade facts stages and rows (staged handling for a puppy, stop if the dog is distressed). The one cause this card makes: a dog that needs the groom paced to it. Behaviour led. On Puppy grooming and Mobile dog grooming this card is the page's main angle: what a first session covers (the table, the brush, the dryer, without a full trim) or what a visit at home takes away (the drive, the waiting, other dogs). On Cat grooming it says when a vet is the right place for the cat (a coat that needs clipping off; sedation is never a groomer's decision). Principles, never this business's practice unless a confirmed practice says so. No guarantee that the dog settles or ends up liking it.
cards.mechanism: a dog that needs the groom paced to it

cards.title: Why a brush or a bath at home isn't the same
cards.brief: What home tools do not reach, from the trade facts methods cell and facts rows for this service: a brush that only touches the top coat, a towel that leaves the roots damp, clippers that shorten a wiry coat yet leave the dead hair in place, a shave that does not stop shedding, nails that can only be shortened gradually. The one cause this card makes: home tools not reaching the undercoat, the dead coat or the skin. Care led. Said as the reason the service exists, never as a telling off. Never instructions for cutting mats or nails at home. Not the coat type (card 1) and not a slipped routine (card 2).
cards.mechanism: home tools not reaching the undercoat, the dead coat or the skin

cards.title: What the local walks bring home
cards.brief: Coats caked in clay through the winter, salt and sand driven right down into a thick coat after the beach, grit between the pads from the pavements. The one cause this card makes: the ground the town's dogs are walked on; the town profile says which (farmland footpaths and bridleways, a beach, heathland, a river bank, gritted streets). Say plainly what that does to the groom: the rinse and the drying a salty or muddy coat needs, the paws checked. Describes the walks, never how well kept any particular dog is, and never a parasite or an outbreak. Not matting or shedding as such: the town's category and service pages own those.
cards.mechanism: the ground the town's dogs are walked on

cards.title: Seeds and grit in paws and ears
cards.brief: A dog that chews its paws after a summer walk, a spaniel shaking its head, grit packed between the pads in winter. The one cause this card makes: what gets caught in feathering, ears and between the toes on the town's walks; the town profile gives the long grass, heath, verges or gritted pavements. Say what the groom looks for and clears (the paw check, the outside of the ears, the feathering trimmed where agreed), from the trade facts stages. A sore ear or a limp is a reason to see a vet: say so, name no condition. Not the mud and salt on the coat: card 1 owns that.
cards.mechanism: what gets caught in feathering, ears and between the toes

cards.title: Nowhere at home to wash a dog
cards.brief: A flat with no outside tap, a terraced house with a small bathroom, a big dog and a small shower. The one cause this card makes: homes with no room to wash and dry a dog properly, so a damp coat gets left; the town profile gives the housing (flats, terraces, new estates). Say what a salon or a van at the door gives such a home, in plain words, and where LINKABLE PAGES has the town's mobile grooming page or its bath service page, link one. Never that the owner has neglected the dog. Not a coat not dried to the skin: the category page owns that.
cards.mechanism: homes with no room to wash and dry a dog

cards.title: Dogs that don't travel well to a salon
cards.brief: An older dog stiff after the car, a nervous rescue that shakes in a waiting room, a household with three dogs and one car, an owner without transport. The one cause this card makes: the journey and the waiting room being harder on the dog than the groom; the town profile may say who lives here (retired owners, young families with crossbreeds, homes out in the country a long way from any salon). Behaviour led. Say what suits such dogs from the services the client offers only (a visit at home where Mobile dog grooming is on the services list, a quiet appointment otherwise), from confirmed practices; no guarantee of a calm dog. Not too much at once in the salon: the category page owns that.
cards.mechanism: the journey and the waiting room being harder than the groom

cards.title: Getting a van to your door
cards.brief: Only where Mobile dog grooming is on the services list: the travel, and where a van can be parked and kept running, from the trade facts price row (travel and access, parking, water and power on board). Terraced streets with no parking, flats with no bay and long rural drives each change it; the town profile says which. Never a rule about parking as the customer's homework. No figure. Where the client has no mobile service, this card is the distance from the salon only from [CV: travel_distance], else how the dog gets there is left to the owner and the card says nothing about travel cost.

cards.title: What the walks round here do to a coat
cards.brief: A coat that comes in wetter, muddier or saltier takes more brushing, rinsing and drying: the trade facts price row for the bath (dense or dirty coat, longer brushing and drying). Say it plainly from the town profile where it gives the walks. No figure, and never that dogs here are dirtier than elsewhere.

cards.title: The first groom after a long gap
cards.brief: A coat left since the last groom, or a dog new to grooming, is a longer first appointment than the ones that follow: the trade facts price rows (matting needing a clip off, familiarisation and breaks). Said without unkindness and never as the owner's failure; no figure; not the service pages' coat on the day card in the same words.

cards.title: Size, coat and temperament
cards.brief: A bigger dog, a thicker or longer coat, and a dog that needs breaks and slower handling each take longer: the first factors in the trade facts price rows. Say it plainly as the dog's needs; no figure. Code adds the price line from [CV: price_list] when there is one.

faq_slots.question: How much does [WORK_LOWER] cost in [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Prices only from [CV: price_list]; otherwise how the price is reached, from [CV: quote_method] only, and that the figure is agreed before the groom when that practice is confirmed. One factor at most (travel for a visit at home, only where Mobile dog grooming is offered), never the list again.

faq_slots.question: How soon can you fit a dog in from [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: start_time] and [CV: response_time] only. The town is in the area covered; nothing about distance unless [CV: travel_distance] is set.

faq_slots.question: Do you cover [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Yes: the town and the villages around it (code lists them; name none). Whether that means a visit at home or a drive to the salon only from the services list and the client values. Link one page in this town.

faq_slots.question: Are you insured to look after my dog?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The cover figure from [CV: insurance_cover] and what the cover is for: the dogs in the business's care, as the policy names it. Never what it pays or who it covers beyond that.

faq_slots.question: What if my dog doesn't settle?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Open with what happens: the groom slows down, takes a break or stops rather than forcing the dog, and the owner is called, as the way careful groomers work, drawn from the trade facts rows. Principles, never this business's practice unless a confirmed practice says so. No guarantee of a calm dog. Never invent insurance or a guarantee. Never sedation.

faq_slots.question: How does booking a groom work in [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: quote_method], [CV: access_handling] and the confirmed practices only: what the owner tells us, what is agreed before the groom, where the groom happens (the salon, or at home only where Mobile dog grooming is on the services list), drop off and collection only where the practices say. No timescale unless [CV: response_time] is set. Never a duration.

faq_slots.question: Do you groom dogs in [TOWN] all year round?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Yes: what each season brings to the coat in plain words from the pack's coat year (the undercoat coming away as the weather warms and cools, seeds in the warm months, mud and grit in the cold ones) and what the groom does about it. No dates, no promise of a slot. A visit at home in bad weather only from the confirmed practices.
